title: Multiplexing fluorogenic esterase-based viability assay with luciferase assays
author: Ohgane, Yoshioka, et al.

steps.title: Seed cells in 96‑well plate
steps.instruction: Plate the luciferase‑expressing cell line in a white 96‑well clear‑bottomed plate at 100 µL per well using a cell density appropriate for the luciferase assay; incubate in a humidified CO₂ incubator until cells adhere (appropriate time).

steps.title: Treat cells with compounds (optional)
steps.instruction: If required, add test compounds to the wells and incubate for the desired treatment time.

steps.title: Prepare working solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare a 20 µM CytoRed working solution containing 1 % Triton X‑100 and a D‑luciferin working solution as described in the recipes section; protect both solutions from light and use within 1 hour.

steps.title: Remove culture medium
steps.instruction: Aspirate the medium from each well using an aspirator equipped with a multichannel adaptor; proceed to the next step within a few minutes to prevent cell drying.

steps.title: Add CytoRed and record initial fluorescence
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL per well of the CytoRed working solution with a multichannel pipette and reagent reservoir; immediately measure fluorescence on a microplate reader (excitation 570 nm, emission 615 nm, bottom‑read mode, e.g., PerkinElmer EnVision).

steps.title: Incubate and measure CytoRed fluorescence
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate at room temperature or 37 °C for 10 minutes, then measure fluorescence again under the same settings. For analysis, subtract the initial fluorescence from the 10‑minute reading (or use the reader’s kinetic mode). Note: longer incubation weakens subsequent luminescence.

steps.title: Add luciferin and record luminescence
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL per well of the luciferin working solution; after a 1‑minute incubation, measure luminescence on the same plate reader in ultra‑sensitive luminescence mode with a 10 ms exposure. The glow‑type signal persists for >10 minutes but gradually declines.
